newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BERTELSMANN AG, PEARSON BID FOR HUNGARY TV - AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: BERTELSMANN AG, PEARSON BID FOR HUNGARY TV - AGENCY.

text.p: Bertelsmann AG and Pearson PLC are involved in a joint venture bid for a Hungarian television channel, Hungarian telecommunications company Matav said on Monday.

Matav, in a statement carried by Hungarian news agency MTI, said that CLT-UFA, which is 50 percent owned by Bertelsmann, along with Matav, Pearson and Raiffeisen Unicbank had formed a joint venture company called M-RTL to bid for the channel.
The joint venture is headed by CLT-UFA, which owns 49 percent of the new company, while Matav has a 25 percent stake and Pearson has 20 percent.
Matav officials could not be reached for comment.
Pearson Television plans to set up a new Hungarian unit to produce programmes for the channel, MTI reported.

Hungary's radio and television body ORTT said on April 10 it had received three bids for two commercial TV channels offered for 10-year concessions but did not announce the names of the bidders at the time.

Foreign companies said to be lining up for concessions to run the channels, which attracted $200 million in advertising fees last year, included U.S.-based Central European Media Enterprises, CLT-Bertelsmann, Hungarian-Swedish consortium MTM-SBS and a consortium of French channel TF1 and Germany's Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung.
Under Hungary's media law, bids have to be evaluated within 60 days and winners have to go on the air three months after contracts are signed.
